chapterNote: The last psalm, and the Psalter's grand finale — thirteen hallelujahs in six verses, the book's entire journey of laments, confessions, curses, and thanksgivings resolving into one unbroken chord of praise. It answers every question a worshiper could ask. Where? In His sanctuary below and in the mighty expanse of His heavens above — earth and sky as one auditorium. Why? For His mighty acts, and according to the measure of His surpassing greatness — praise proportioned not to our mood but to His magnitude. With what? The whole orchestra, listed instrument by instrument: ram's horn, harp and lyre, tambourine and dancing, strings and pipe, cymbals loud and cymbals crashing — priest's trumpet and shepherd's flute, sanctuary and street, everything that can make a sound conscripted. And who? The widest summons in the Bible: let everything that has breath praise the LORD — every creature still drawing the breath God breathed into it owes the air back as praise. The Psalter's last word is its first duty and its final destiny: Hallelujah.

1.text: Praise the LORD! Praise God in His sanctuary; praise Him in the mighty expanse of His power!
1.amp: Praise ye the LORD ['Hallelujah', halal Yah, the KJV margin]. Praise [halal] God [El] in His sanctuary [qodesh]: praise Him in the firmament [raqia — the expanse] of His power [oz].
1.notes: halelu-Yah (H1984, H3050): the imperative that gave every language its 'hallelujah'. The two venues span everything: the qodesh (H6944), the sanctuary below, and the raqia oz (H7549, H5797), the mighty expanse above — the same firmament that declares His glory in Psalm 19 now hosting the choir.

2.text: Praise Him for His deeds of might; praise Him in the measure of His abounding greatness!
2.amp: Praise [halal] Him for His mighty acts [geburah]: praise Him according to His excellent [rob] greatness [godel].
2.notes: The two grounds of praise: His geburot (H1369), the mighty deeds history records, and His godel (H1433), the greatness He simply is. 'According to' sets the measure — praise scaled to rob (H7230), abundance: since His greatness has no ceiling, neither does the singing.

3.text: Praise Him with the blast of the ram's horn; praise Him with the harp and the lyre!
3.amp: Praise [halal] Him with the sound [teqa — the blast] of the trumpet [shophar — the ram's horn]: praise Him with the psaltery [nebel — the harp] and harp [kinnor — the lyre].
3.notes: The orchestra assembles from the top: the shophar (H7782), the ram's horn that announced jubilee and coronation — the priest's instrument — then nebel and kinnor (H5035, H3658), David's own strings. Proclamation and melody, the loud and the lovely, both drafted.

4.text: Praise Him with the tambourine and dancing; praise Him with strings and pipe!
4.amp: Praise [halal] Him with the timbrel [toph — the tambourine] and dance [machol — 'or, pipe', the KJV margin]: praise Him with stringed instruments [minnim] and organs [ugab — the flute, the pipe].
4.notes: The music leaves the platform for the street: the toph (H8596) was the women's instrument — Miriam's at the sea (cf. Exodus 15:20) — and machol (H4234) is the dance itself: the body joins the orchestra. minnim and ugab (H4482, H5748), strings and shepherd's pipe: folk instruments, everyman's praise.

5.text: Praise Him with resounding cymbals; praise Him with the crashing cymbals of the shout!
5.amp: Praise [halal] Him upon the loud [shema — sounding, heard afar] cymbals [tseltselim]: praise Him upon the high sounding [teruah — the shout, the blast] cymbals.
5.notes: tseltselim (H6767) twice — the ringing pair and the crashing pair, cymbals of hearing and cymbals of teruah (H8643), the shout-word of battle and coronation. The Psalter's last instrument is its least subtle: praise that can be heard from a distance, unembarrassed.

6.text: Let every thing that draws breath praise the LORD! Hallelujah — praise the LORD!
6.amp: Let every thing that has breath [neshamah — the breath of life] praise [halal] the LORD [Yah]. Praise ye the LORD [halelu-Yah].
6.notes: The final summons is the widest: kol ha-neshamah (H5397) — everything carrying the breath God breathed into Adam (cf. Genesis 2:7). Breath is borrowed; praise is the rent. And the Psalter's very last word is its whole theology in two syllables: halelu-Yah — the word now sung around the throne without end (cf. Revelation 19:1-6).
